# ECN-2026-008 - Change notice - Machining CNC turning center #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line: P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: During a recent preventive maintenance review and spindle rebuild on Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03), maintenance personnel discovered inconsistent clamp preload on the chuck jaws after routine reassembly. The root cause analysis identified that the previous standard referenced an incorrect torque value for the chuck jaw bolts in the equipment-specific maintenance checklist. The incorrect torque resulted in uneven jaw seating, intermittent concentricity loss on turned parts, and increased wear on the collet and jaw interface. To mitigate the risk of part nonconformance, reduced tool life, and potential safety hazards from loose hardware, the chuck jaw bolt torque specification is being corrected.

Change summary: Update the specified chuck jaw bolt torque for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to the correct value: 95 N·m. This ECN updates applicable maintenance procedures, inspection checkpoints, and training material references to reflect the corrected torque value and adds a verification step in the reassembly sign-off process.

Affected items
--------------
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03 (Machining CNC turning center #3) — torque specification for chuck jaw bolts.  
- Documentation: Maintenance checklist and work instructions that reference chuck jaw bolt torque for EQ-P1-L3-CN03. Refer to SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, and SOP-P1-L3-03 for linked procedures and baseline records.  
- Spare parts handling: Any spare chuck jaw bolt replacements used during maintenance must be torqued to 95 N·m when installed on EQ-P1-L3-CN03.  
- Quality inspections: In-process first-article checks and in-shift chuck verification routines that sample turned parts from EQ-P1-L3-CN03.

Implementation
--------------
Scope: Applies to all maintenance and assembly activities on EQ-P1-L3-CN03 at plant P1, line P1-L3. The new torque specification replaces the previous value in all equipment-specific documentation and in maintenance task instructions.

Actions:
- Documentation update: Revise the maintenance checklist and torque table entries within SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 to state the chuck jaw bolt torque for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 as 95 N·m. Add a cross-reference note to SB-1014 for spindle rebuild best practices.
- Tooling: Ensure calibrated torque wrenches used for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 are capable of and set to 95 N·m when performing chuck jaw bolt installation. Record calibration status in the tool log for the wrench used.
- Rework and verification: For any unit of EQ-P1-L3-CN03 that has undergone chuck or jaw replacement since the previous specification, perform a re-torque and verification to 95 N·m at the next available maintenance opportunity. Log the re-torque action per the record procedure below.
- Training: Conduct a focused operator and maintenance briefing covering the revised torque requirement and the rationale. Include a hands-on session during which personnel practice the re-torque and verification steps using the documented checklist.
- Sign-off procedure: Add a mandatory sign-off line to the maintenance work order that records: technician name, torque applied (95 N·m), torque tool identifier, and witness inspector initials. The witness inspector must be a qualified maintenance lead or quality engineer.
- Inspection sampling: Increase first-piece inspection attention after reassembly. Typical checks include concentricity and runout assessments as defined in SB-1014 and related SOPs. If out-of-spec conditions are found, retain the assembly and follow nonconformance procedures.

Step rationale and examples:
- Rationale: Achieving uniform preload on all chuck jaw bolts ensures even jaw seating and consistent clamping force. This reduces part runout and vibration, preserves jaw and spindle interfaces, and minimizes risk of bolt loosening. A comparative example: an assembly torqued uniformly to the specified value produced repeatable concentricity across multiple part families, whereas assemblies with variable torque showed intermittent high runout on semi-critical diameters.
- Example work step: After cleaning mating surfaces and applying thread lock where specified in SB-1014, hand-start all chuck jaw bolts, then tighten in the manufacturer-recommended sequence to bring them up evenly. Final torque each bolt to 95 N·m using a calibrated torque wrench while a witness observes and signs the work order.

Records to keep
---------------
Maintain the following records in the equipment maintenance folder and the electronic document control system:
- Updated copies of SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 with the 95 N·m entry.  
- Maintenance work orders showing re-torque actions to 95 N·m, including technician and witness signatures and torque tool identifier.  
- Torque wrench calibration certificate for the tool used, retained per calibration schedule and linked to the work order.  
- Post-reassembly inspection reports and first-article inspection records referencing SB-1014 where applicable.  
- Training attendance and competency sign-off records for personnel who performed or supervised the re-torque work.

Approvals
---------
The following approvals are required to close this ECN and implement the change in production:
- Maintenance Manager approval for revision of SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 to include the 95 N·m value.  
- Quality Manager approval for updated inspection checkpoints and first-article criteria referencing SB-1014.  
- Operations Manager acknowledgement of the updated sign-off and training requirements for EQ-P1-L3-CN03.

Post-implementation review
--------------------------
After implementation, conduct a focused review to confirm effectiveness: review maintenance logs and inspection results for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 for at least one production cycle following the change, verify that all re-torque records to 95 N·m are complete, and ensure no related part nonconformances are reported. If issues persist, escalate per SB-1014 and update SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 as required.

Related documents
-----------------
SB-1014  
SOP-P1-L3-02  
SOP-P1-L3-03

Prepared by: Maintenance Engineering  
Distribution: Plant P1 maintenance, quality, and operations records systems
